channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Indian Rupee plummets as renewed Middle East conflicts boost oil prices
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) starts the week on a negative note against the US Dollar (USD), with the USD/INR pair jumping to near 95.65.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: At two-month highs, with 0.8000 in focus
item.description: The US Dollar is rallying for the second consecutive day against the Swiss Franc (CHF) on Monday, reaching levels near 0.8000 for the first time in the last two months.

item.title: US President Trump urges Israel and Iran to pause attacks immediately
item.description: United States (US) President Donald urges Iran and Israel to pause the exchange of attacks, through a post on Truth Social, during the European trading session on Monday.

item.title: British Pound: Seen lower against Euro and US Dollar – ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner expects the Bank of England (BoE) to avoid tightening this year, with only modest rate hikes priced by markets.

item.title: Euro edges lower vs Japanese Yen as BoJ tightening bets support JPY
item.description: EUR/JPY trades around 184.10 on Monday at the time of writing, down 0.32% on the day, as the Japanese Yen (JPY) continues to benefit from a favorable backdrop driven by expectations of higher interest rates in Japan and renewed warnings from Japanese authorities regarding currency weakness.

item.title: Indian Rupee: Inflow tools preferred over hikes – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Charlie Lay highlights that the Reserve Bank of India kept its policy rate at 5.25% and signalled a preference to bolster the Rupee via capital inflow measures rather than tightening.

item.title: US Dollar: Crossroads for policy and geopolitics – HSBC
item.description: HSBC’s FX Viewpoint highlights that the US Dollar sits at a crossroads, driven by Middle East tensions, US trade policy shifts and the upcoming June Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) under new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver falls, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) fell on Monday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $67.02 per troy ounce, down 1.21% from the $67.84 it cost on Friday.

item.title: Euro: ECB hike but growth worries – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Bob Savage notes that an European Central Bank (ECB) rate hike is widely expected, but guidance on future moves and growth risks will be crucial for EUR/USD.

item.title: Oil: Price jumps on Iran conflict escalation – Danske Bank
item.description: Danske Research Team notes that Brent Oil has surged toward USD 96 per barrel after renewed Israel–Iran hostilities, with markets reassessing regional supply risks. They highlight that the latest air strikes have undermined hopes for a broader deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Rate expectations cap gains against US Dollar – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s Elias Haddad (BBH) expects the Bank of Canada to keep its policy rate at 2.25% and maintain two-way optionality, as contained inflation allows an extended pause.

item.title: Euro advances against Canadian Dollar despite higher oil prices
item.description: EUR/CAD inches higher after registering over 0.5% losses in the previous day, trading around 1.6070 during the European hours on Monday. The currency cross gains some ground as the commodity-linked Canadian Dollar (CAD) struggles despite higher oil prices.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Risk extends toward 0.7000 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann flag that AUD/USD posted its second-largest one‑day loss of the year, dropping toward 0.7040. Near term, the pair may test 0.7020, though a sustained break below is seen as unlikely.

item.title: Euro languishes near two-month lows on higher Oil prices, weak Eurozone data
item.description: The Euro (EUR) consolidates losses against the US Dollar (USD) on Monday, trading at 1.1515 at the time of writing, following a 0.75% sell-off on Friday.

item.title: USD/JPY: Yield spread keeps pair on upward path – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale analysts say USD/JPY has rebounded after defending a multi‑month ascending trend line around 155.50/155.00 and is now challenging the April high. Support is seen at 159.20, with projections at 161.20 and 162.

item.title: IRGC retaliates by attacking petrochemical site in northern Israeli city of Haifa
item.description: According to the Fars news agency, Iran’s Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) has confirmed attacking a petrochemical site in northern Israeli city of Haifa, in retaliation for Israel’s attack on a similar plant in Iran, The Guardian reported.

item.title: Experts agree: The Indian Rupee enjoys a short-term respite that may not last
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) is receiving a notable boost following the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) monetary policy meeting on Friday, when policymakers unanimously decided to hold the benchmark repo rate steady at 5.25%.

item.title: US Dollar: Positioning stays supportive – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank strategists Molly Schwartz and Jane Foley highlight that USD net long futures positioning has more than quadrupled, reflecting resilient support for the Dollar.

item.title: Eurozone Sentix Investor Confidence improves to -13.4 in June
item.description: Eurozone’s Sentix Investor Confidence data, a key indicator of Investor morale, improves to -13.4 in June from -16.4 in May.

item.title: Gold sticks to losses below $4,300, lowest since March as inflation fears bolster Fed bets
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) maintains its offered tone through the first half of the European session on Monday and currently trades just below the $4,300 mark – the lowest since March 23.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD holds losses near $67.00 as Middle East tensions escalate
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) extends its losses for the second successive day, trading around $67.00 per troy ounce during the European hours on Monday.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Warsh debut raises independence questions – DBS
item.description: Philip Wee at DBS Group Research highlights that Kevin Warsh’s first meeting as Fed Chair will be critical for perceptions of Federal Reserve independence. Warsh must reconcile President Trump’s push for rate cuts with a more data-dependent, hawkish FOMC.

item.title: WTI Oil holds near $92.50 as tensions flare up in the Middle East
item.description: Crude prices have jumped by more than $4 on Monday, with the US benchmark West Texas Intermediate (WTI) barrel trading at $92.52 at the time of writing, as tensions between Israel and Iran flare, adding new strains to an already fragile ceasefire in the area.

item.title: European Central Bank: Gradual rate hike path, cuts next year – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Rainer Guntermann says a 25bp ECB hike on Thursday is almost certain and fully priced, marking the first increase since September 2023. He expects no back-to-back move in July, viewing that as premature, but looks for another hike in September.

item.title: GBP/USD Price Forecast: More downside looks likely towards 1.3240
item.description: The GBP/USD pair trades marginally lower to near 1.3338 during the European trading session on Monday. The pair posts a fresh almost three-week low near 1.3316 in the day, as the US Dollar (USD) outperforms amid growing expectations that the Federal Reserve (Fed) will raise interest rates this year.

item.title: Euro: Hawkish ECB may not stop downside pressure versus US Dollar – ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner notes EUR/USD was hit hard as the Dollar surged, increasing pressure on the European Central Bank to sound hawkish while delivering a 25bp hike to 2.25%.

item.title: Dow Jones futures decline as renewed Middle East tensions weigh on market mood
item.description: Dow Jones futures decline 0.33% to near 50,750 during the European hours on Monday, ahead of the US regular opening. However, S&P 500 futures gain 0.10% to near 7,410 and Nasdaq 100 futures rise 0.35%, trading near 29,130 at the time of writing.

item.title: British Pound holds above one-week low vs JPY; intervention risks cap further gains
item.description: The GBP/JPY cross stages a modest recovery from over a one-week low, around the 213.30 region touched earlier this Monday, and sticks to modest intraday gains through the first half of the European session.

item.title: Indian Rupee: RBI flow measures offer near-term support – OCBC
item.description: OCBC reports that the Reserve Bank of India kept its policy rate at 5.25% but unveiled targeted capital flow measures, including concessional FX swaps and tax exemptions for foreign investors in government bonds.

item.title: Iran holds US responsible for recent ceasefire breaches
item.description: According to an Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson, Esmail Baghaei, the United States (US) is responsible for the recent ceasefire breaches. “The actions of the Zionist entity within the region cannot be looked at in isolation from the United States, Baghaei said.
